Riding light (first light to last light, Vancouver): Fri, Oct 23 7:13am to 6:40pm; Sat, Oct 24 7:14am to 6:38pm; Sun, Oct 25 7:16am to 6:36pm. Hours outside that are dark and not listed; never suggest riding then.

Guillermo's own take for Fri, Oct 23 (his read, quote it as his, not yours): The northwest is easing faster than I hoped. The Ferry Terminal dropped from 15 at 6am to 11 at 8am, and the tide is now too low on the south side until about 11:30am. I’m calling Tsawwassen off.

The only maybe is Porteau. Pam Rocks is building from the north, 12 at 8am, and the tide bottoms at 7.5ft around 10am. If Pam Rocks reads 22+ before 10am, go. Otherwise it fades by late morning.

Skipping Squamish: the valley is 6°C colder than Pam Rocks and Pemberton is still 2 hPa above Vancouver.

EC marine forecast, Howe Sound (issued 09:30 PM PDT 23 October 2026), WARNING IN EFFECT: Tonight and Saturday. Strong wind warning in effect. Wind northerly outflow 15 knots increasing to northerly outflow 20 near noon Saturday and to northerly outflow 20 to 30 early Saturday evening.

EC marine forecast, Strait of Georgia (south of Nanaimo) (issued 09:30 PM PDT 23 October 2026): Tonight and Saturday. Wind light increasing to southeast 10 to 15 knots near midnight and to easterly 15 to 20 early Saturday afternoon.

Track record, last 30 days: Porteau Cove (scored at Pam Rocks): typical miss 3.31kt, caught 53% of windy hours, 13% false alarms; Steveston - Garry Point Park (scored at Sand Heads): typical miss 2.56kt, caught 80% of windy hours, 23% false alarms; Tsawwassen Ferry Terminal Causeway (scored at Tsawwassen Ferry Terminal): typical miss 2.89kt, caught 65% of windy hours, 32% false alarms; Erwin Park (scored at Point Atkinson): typical miss 2.72kt, caught 41% of windy hours, 17% false alarms.
